meta.titre: Verb Tenses: perfect and continuous forms, time clues and tense changes

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A bus driver leaving Douala tells his passengers, "By the time we reach Bafoussam, we will have been travelling for six hours." In one sentence he uses a tense that looks forward to a future moment and measures a period of time up to it. At A Level, grammar items rarely test the simple present or past: they test perfect and continuous forms, the choice between them, and the ability to change one form into another. A learner who masters the time clues in the sentence can choose the right tense in seconds.

items: A verb has a base form, a simple past form and a past participle (write, wrote, written).
The simple present, simple past and simple future are formed with the verb alone or with will.
The auxiliary verbs be, have and will help to form other tenses.

sections.titre: Verb tenses: the perfect tenses and the clues that decide the choice
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The perfect tenses and the clues that call for them
| Tense | Form | Main use | Typical clues |
|---|---|---|---|
| Present perfect | has/have + past participle | an action linked to now, or continuing up to now | already, yet, just, ever, never, since, for |
| Present perfect continuous | has/have been + -ing | an action continuing up to now, stressing duration | for two hours, since morning, all day |
| Past perfect | had + past participle | an action completed before another past action or time | before, after, already, by the time |
| Past perfect continuous | had been + -ing | duration up to a past moment | for, since |
| Future perfect | will have + past participle | an action completed before a future moment | by next year, by the time |
| Future perfect continuous | will have been + -ing | duration up to a future moment | by December, for ten years |

### Rules that decide the choice
- **for** + a length of time; **since** + a starting point. Both need a perfect tense in the main clause: "She has taught here since 2015."
- A finished time word (yesterday, last week, in 2015, ago) requires the simple past, never the present perfect.
- A **by + future time** phrase calls for the future perfect: "By next June, the school will have admitted two hundred pupils."
- In a time clause (when, before, after, as soon as, until, by the time) and in an if-clause, use the present simple for the future, not will: "By the time we arrive, the match will have started."
- **Stative verbs** (know, believe, belong, own, want, understand) are normally not used in continuous forms: say "I have known him for years".
- With verbs such as live, work and teach the simple and continuous perfect forms are close in meaning. The continuous form stresses duration up to the point in question; use the other clues in the item to decide.

### Past participles to master
| Base | Past | Past participle |
|---|---|---|
| write | wrote | written |
| eat | ate | eaten |
| fly | flew | flown |
| choose | chose | chosen |
| begin | began | begun |
| swim | swam | swum |
| take | took | taken |
| speak | spoke | spoken |

variantes.nom: Gap-filling and multiple choice by time clues
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a sentence has a gap and several tense options.
variantes.contenu_markdown: 1. Find the time word (by, since, for, already, when). 2. Decide whether the action is before, at or after the reference moment. 3. Ask whether the sentence stresses duration (for, since, all day). 4. Eliminate options that break a rule, for example will after by the time, then choose among those that remain.

variantes.nom: Transforming verbs (for example into the past perfect)
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to pick out verbs and change their tense.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Find the base verb, keep the subject, and build the new form: past perfect = **had** + past participle. For example "walks" becomes "had walked" and "broke" becomes "had broken". The auxiliary had does not change with the subject. For a passive or negative verb, change only the auxiliary: "was built" becomes "had been built".

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the sentence has if, or when direct speech is turned into reported speech.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Third conditional: **if + past perfect, would have + past participle** ("If she had left earlier, she would have caught the bus"). Reported speech after a past reporting verb moves one step back: simple past becomes past perfect, "will" becomes "would". "I have finished," he said becomes He said he had finished.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Fill each gap with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

(a) By the time the bus reaches Bamenda tonight, the passengers ______ (travel) for nine hours.
(b) When the inspector arrived, the headmaster ______ (already, leave) the office.
(c) Nobody ______ (see) Mr Tanyi since he travelled to Kumba.
(d) If you ______ (study) harder last term, you would have passed the exam.

etapes.action: Mark the time clues in each sentence.
etapes.justification: The clue tells you which point in time the verb refers to.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) "By the time ... reaches" and "for nine hours"; (b) "When ... arrived" and "already"; (c) "since he travelled"; (d) "if", "last term" and "would have passed".

etapes.justification: The bus has not yet reached Bamenda, so the reference moment is in the future; the sentence measures a period up to it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Future perfect continuous: **will have been travelling**. The clause "reaches" is in the present simple because it follows "by the time".

etapes.justification: There are two past actions. Leaving the office happened before the inspector arrived.
In (c), since + a simple past clause needs a perfect tense in the main clause. In (d), the result clause "would have passed" signals the third conditional.
Common faults are will after by the time or if, and a wrong participle.
etapes.resultat_markdown: None of the gaps contains will after a time or if clause. The participles seen and studied are correct.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) will have been travelling (the simple form will have travelled is also grammatical, but the continuous form stresses the duration); (b) had already left; (c) has seen; (d) had studied.

items.pourquoi_faux: A present tense cannot be used with since. Since needs a perfect tense in the main clause.
items.correction_markdown: "I **have been living** in Douala since 2019" or "I have lived in Douala since 2019".

items.erreur_markdown: "By the time we will arrive, the film will have started."
items.pourquoi_faux: After by the time, when, before, until and if, the present simple expresses the future; will is not used.
items.correction_markdown: "By the time we **arrive**, the film will have started."

items.erreur_markdown: "She has been knowing the answer for a long time."
items.pourquoi_faux: Know is a stative verb and does not normally take a continuous form.
items.correction_markdown: "She **has known** the answer for a long time."

items.erreur_markdown: "If I would have known, I would have told you."
items.pourquoi_faux: Would is not used in the if-clause of the third conditional; the if-clause takes the past perfect.
items.correction_markdown: "If I **had known**, I would have told you."

items.pourquoi_faux: Yesterday is a finished time, and the present perfect is not used with a finished time.

items.enonce_markdown:
Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

(a) Esther ______ (live) in Buea since 2018.
(b) The lesson had already begun when the principal ______ (enter).
(c) By next July, they ______ (build) the new bridge.
(d) We ______ (not, see) our cousins for three years.
items.solution_markdown: **(a) has lived** (or has been living): since needs a perfect tense. **(b) entered**: simple past for the later past action. **(c) will have built**: by + future time. **(d) have not seen** (or haven't seen): for + a period up to now.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Write the past perfect, third person singular, of each verb: write, eat, fly, choose, begin, swim.
(b) Join each pair into one sentence beginning with "By the time", using the past perfect for the earlier action.
   (i) The guests arrived. The cook finished the meal.
   (ii) The principal entered the hall. The pupils took their seats.
items.solution_markdown:
**(a)** **had written, had eaten, had flown, had chosen, had begun, had swum**.
**(b)(i)** By the time the guests arrived, the cook **had finished** the meal.
**(b)(ii)** By the time the principal entered the hall, the pupils **had taken** their seats.
The earlier action takes the past perfect; the later action stays in the simple past.

items.enonce_markdown:
Fill each numbered gap with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

"By the end of this term, Mr Fon (1) ______ (teach) at the school for thirty years. When he first arrived, the school (2) ______ (not, have) a library, but he (3) ______ (work) tirelessly to raise money, and by 2005 the first books (4) ______ (arrive). If he (5) ______ (give up) during those difficult years, the pupils (6) ______ (never, have) a library."
items.solution_markdown: **(1) will have been teaching** (or will have taught): by + future time plus a duration. **(2) did not have**: simple past for a past state. **(3) worked**: simple past for the past action. **(4) had arrived**: by + a past year calls for the past perfect. **(5) had given up**: if-clause of the third conditional. **(6) would never have had**: result clause of the third conditional.

items_markdown: Read the time clues first: for, since, by, already, when, last year.
Perfect tenses link two moments: the action is complete, or has lasted, up to the reference point.
Past perfect for the earlier of two past actions; future perfect (continuous) for what will be complete (or will have lasted) by a future time.
Never use will after if, when, before, until or by the time: use the present simple.
Stative verbs avoid the continuous form, and a finished time word needs the simple past.
To change a verb into the past perfect, write had + past participle and learn the irregular participles.
